answer: New identities enter as a lotus bud: they may only take tiny, low-value jobs, and each completed job earns a lantern receipt — a public, counterparty-signed record of the work done. Capability grows only as lantern receipts accumulate, like a lotus opening petal by petal. To bid on valuable work, an identity must also lock earned fees in an onyx escrow that is slashed if a counterparty proves fraud. A farm spinning up 1,000 fakes must earn 1,000 separate receipt histories and fund 1,000 escrows, paying full work and collateral per identity, while one honest agent climbs the same ladder once.
